answer: The yard keeper counts every drying mat at dusk and writes the tally in his book, so the leaf spread that day is proved dried mat by mat. A whisper mat claimed as counted fails the tally: the mats must lie in the yard at the willow of the count, and a mat never spread holds no leaf. Forging a drying season means hiring a keeper, faking one hundred tallies and paying 6,700, and the yarrow entry in the book is read at every factory inspection, so leaf whose mats were never counted is left to rot.
